name: Economy
description: Indian economy basics, budget, banking and institutions.

questions.question: Which body replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission, shifting from centralised planning to cooperative federalism.

questions.question: The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) of India prioritised which sector?
questions.explanation: The First Plan focused on agriculture and irrigation, including the Bhakra-Nangal and Damodar Valley projects; heavy industry came with the Second Plan.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution' in India?
questions.explanation: Geneticist M. S. Swaminathan led India's high-yielding wheat revolution in the 1960s; Borlaug developed the dwarf varieties.

questions.question: Operation Flood, the White Revolution that made India the world's largest milk producer, is associated with whom?
questions.explanation: Verghese Kurien's Amul cooperative model powered Operation Flood from 1970, creating the National Dairy Development Board network.

questions.question: The economic liberalisation of 1991 was initiated when Narasimha Rao was PM and who was Finance Minister?
questions.explanation: Dr. Manmohan Singh's July 1991 budget devalued the rupee, dismantled the licence raj and opened India to foreign investment.

questions.question: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures what?
options: Total market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a period
questions.explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a given period (usually a year).

questions.question: GDP at market prices equals which of the following?
options: GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies
GDP at factor cost − indirect taxes + subsidies
GNP + net factor income from abroad
questions.explanation: GDP (market prices) = GDP (factor cost) + indirect taxes − subsidies. GVA is the value-added measure of output.

questions.question: Official GDP and CPI data in India are compiled by which organisation?
questions.explanation: The NSO under the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) compiles GDP, CPI and IIP data.

questions.question: The RBI's inflation-targeting framework mandates a CPI inflation target of what?
questions.explanation: Under the RBI Act (amended 2016), the MPC targets 4% CPI inflation within a tolerance band of 2–6%.

questions.question: The fiscal deficit of the government equals which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total non-debt receipts; it represents the government's total borrowing requirement.

questions.question: Which Act sets fiscal discipline targets (deficit limits) for the Union government?
questions.explanation: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 caps the fiscal deficit and mandates medium-term fiscal statements.

questions.question: Who chairs the GST Council (Article 279A)?
questions.explanation: The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with state finance ministers as members — an example of cooperative federalism.

questions.question: How many main GST rate slabs does India have (excluding zero-rated and special rates)?
questions.explanation: India's GST has four main slabs — 5%, 12%, 18% and 28% — plus exempt and special rates (e.g. 3% for gold).

questions.question: The Sensex is the benchmark index of which stock exchange?
questions.explanation: The Sensex tracks 30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange; the Nifty tracks 50 on the National Stock Exchange.

questions.question: The Nifty 50 index belongs to which exchange?
questions.explanation: The Nifty 50 is the flagship index of the National Stock Exchange, covering 50 of India's largest listed companies.

questions.question: The Gini coefficient is used to measure what?
questions.explanation: The Gini coefficient ranges 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality) and measures the distribution of income or wealth.

questions.question: Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) is used to compare what across countries?
questions.explanation: PPP adjusts GDP comparisons for price differences, showing how much a currency can actually buy in its home country.

questions.question: Which of the following is recorded in a country's current account of the Balance of Payments?
options: Trade in goods and services plus income transfers
questions.explanation: The current account covers exports/imports of goods and services plus income and remittances; capital flows go in the capital account.

questions.question: The Mahatma Gandhi NREGA, guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment per rural household, was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: MGNREGA was passed in 2005 and launched in 200 districts in February 2006, before nationwide expansion.

questions.question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (2018), aimed at transforming backward districts, is run by which body?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme ranks districts on 49 indicators across health, education and infrastructure.
